name: University of the West of England
aliases: Uni of the West of England

settingEvidence.evidence: Our main campus, a 15-minute bus ride from the city centre.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027/28 (up from £9,790 in 2026/27). The government's fee cap is set to rise each year with inflation, so the amount can go up in later years of a course.

source.evidence: Full time tuition fees for 2026/27 will be £9,790 and shall increase to £10,050 for 2027/28.

livingCosts.text: UWE estimates a single student living away from home needs about £14,000–£15,000 per academic year, based on mid-range accommodation (not including tuition fees). The page does not say which academic year this is for.

source.evidence: set aside between £14,000–£15,000 per academic year as a single student, based on mid-range accommodation costs

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days: Saturday 21 November 2026 (on campus, all campuses) and Wednesday 2 December 2026 (online, from 4pm).

contextual.summary: UK (Home) applicants who qualify automatically get a contextual offer 16 UCAS tariff points lower for undergraduate degrees (8 points for foundation year courses), plus UWE's Access to UWE Bristol support programme.
contextual.typicalReduction: 16 UCAS tariff points lower for undergraduate degrees (8 points lower for foundation year courses)

criteria.detail: UWE uses the UCAS Multiple Equality Measure (MEM) to assess eligibility; the page does not publish a MEM threshold.
Caring and parental responsibilities (from the 'More about you' section of the UCAS application form).

Health conditions, learning differences or disabilities (from the 'More about you' section of the UCAS application form).
Refugee status (from the 'More about you' section of the UCAS application form).
Estrangement from parents (from the 'More about you' section of the UCAS application form).

contextual.rulesText: Available to UK (Home) applicants only. UWE uses the UCAS Multiple Equality Measure (MEM) plus the 'More about you' questions on the UCAS form; you do not need to do anything extra except apply through UCAS and complete 'More about you' fully. Contextual offer holders are invited to Access to UWE Bristol (webinars, a free Summer School for offer holders aged 18+, and the Wallscourt Scholarship of £2,000 over three years for 15 contextual offer holders).

source.evidence: Contextual offers are available to UK (Home) applicants only.

notes: All courses use 2027 entry: every course page shows 'Entry year 2027/28'; no 2028 entry pages are published yet (checked 2026-10-21).

UWE makes offers in UCAS tariff points (112 for most of these courses, 120 for Real Estate and Development) and the course pages say no specific A-level subjects are needed. GCSE English and Maths at grade C/4 are required.
UWE is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of these course pages names an admissions test.

Accommodation guarantee: UWE guarantees accommodation to full-time first-year students applying for the first time by the deadline, after accepting UWE as a firm choice (terms published for a September 2027 start; the room may be in the city centre).
Courses are taught at the Frenchay Campus (about 15 minutes by bus from Bristol city centre). Foundation year versions exist for most of these courses under their own UCAS codes.
